thread:
Diego: Hey team, since ~09:10 UTC our tenant vertex-labs is getting a ton of 429s on their Dedicated pool (ded-88-eu-central). User reports and our monitors show throughput collapse.
Sara: Sorry — can you drop a couple sample request IDs and when you first saw it?
Diego: reqs: `a7d1c9`, `a7d1ca`, `a7d1ff` around 2026-03-17T09:10:07Z. Responses include metadata "throttled: pool_quota".
Sara: Copying @Josh @Priya. Are they on reserved capacity or shared bursting?
Diego: Reserved (committed). Typical avg is ~90 rps for them. This looks new.
Josh: Checking control plane logs for those req ids now. Preliminary: routing resolved tenant to pool `ded-12-small` with tier set to `standard` even though tenant should be `enterprise`. That mismatch would push them into a small pool and cause the 429s.
Priya: That implies the tier resolution step returned default. Any recent changes in routing/policy? @Josh
Alex: Also noticed a short noisy neighbor event on ded-12 earlier which may have suppressed autoscaler, but wrong pool selection is the root here.
Josh: We rolled out a key normalization patch at 08:20 UTC that lowercases route cache keys. The policy lookup expects DB label keys in TitleCase. If header provides `X-Tenant-Tier: Enterprise` we normalize to `x-tenant-tier` and then cache lookup misses; fallback rule picks `standard` tier.
Sara: Diego, what's in your inbound context? header example is fine.
Diego: We send:
```
X-Tenant-ID: vertex-labs
X-Tenant-Tier: Enterprise
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```
Priya: Repro locally hitting /resolve with that header — new behavior returns small pool.
```
# repro
curl -H "X-Tenant-ID: vertex-labs" -H "X-Tenant-Tier: Enterprise" https://control.internal/resolve
# before patch -> pool ded-88-eu-central
# after patch -> pool ded-12-small
```
Alex: Runtime returned `POOL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED` in logs for those requests. So everything aligns.
Josh: Mitigation options:
- rollback the normalization change (fast but noisy)
- deploy a quick compatibility layer that checks both lowercased and TitleCase cache keys (medium)
- create an explicit routing override mapping for vertex-labs -> ded-88-eu-central (fastest, targeted)
Priya: I'll push an override map entry now for the impacted tenants while we work on a fix.
deploy-bot: Override applied: tenant `vertex-labs` -> pool `ded-88-eu-central` by Priya at 2026-03-17T09:31:14Z :white_check_mark:
Sara: Diego, can you retry a few calls now?
Diego: Retried at 09:31:40Z: sample req `a7d200` returned 200, latency back to expected levels.
Josh: Good. I'm preparing a rollback PR as insurance. Long-term fix: make policy engine tolerant of casing and canonicalize consistently against DB labels.
Alex: I'll also add a metric that correlates routing mismatches with autoscaler suppression events so we can detect compound failures.
Priya: Action items:
- P0: Deploy tolerant key lookup (owner: Priya) ETA 3h
- P1: Rollback PR queued (owner: Josh) ETA 45m
- P1: Customer comms and incident note (owner: Sara) ETA 1h
- P2: Autoscale suppression audit (owner: Alex) ETA 1d
Sara: I'll notify the customer and mark as escalated. Diego — ping me if there are billing hits due to the 429 window and we'll review credits.
Diego: Thanks for the quick patch. Please keep me updated on the permanent fix timeline.
Josh: Saved trace id `tr-20260317-09-10-vertex` and rule logs for RCA:
```
RULE-EVAL: tenant=vertex-labs header=X-Tenant-Tier=Enterprise normalized_key=x-tenant-tier cache_miss -> db_label_key='TenantTier' present -> mismatch -> default_tier=standard
```
Priya: I'll post a short incident note in #postmortems with tenant list and remediation steps after the patch deploys. Closing updates here once patch is live.
Sara: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
